messages.subject: TerraClimate
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I've just made a new function, 'micro_terra <https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/blob/master/R/micro_terra.R>', which connects to the TerraClimate <https://www.climatologylab.org/terraclimate.html> data set of monthly climate at ~4km res across the globe from 1958 to present (well, 2020).

There are also climate change scenarios of +2 and +4 deg C. You can use them by setting the input parameter 'scenario' to 2 or 4.

It connects to the TerraClimate data via opendap and is pretty quick to download, but slower for the climate change scenarios (which are imposed on the years 1985 to 2015).

You can set 'elevatr = 1' to download a finer res DEM than the 4km one and then adjust for lapse rate, as well as slope/aspect/horizon angle if 'terrain = 1'. Also, you can use the microclima solar radiation algorithm to adjust hourly solar if 'microclima = 1'.

If you want to simulate snow or soil moisture properly, you should set 'timeinterval = 365', which will interpolate the monthly data to daily.

Let me know if you find any issues with it.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Upper Critical Temperature
messages.body_plain:
Hey Mike,

I was hoping you could clarify some terminology. I've been trying to locate the right numbers to input for TC_MAX on some species, and I've been running into upper critical temperature (UCT). Some sources are saying it's the maximum body temperature that can be tolerated by an organism, which would suggest that it is the parameter I'm looking for. However, other sources are specifying that it's just the upper bound of the thermo-neutral zone, which would suggest that it isn't TC_MAX (particularly since in some cases the reported UCT is lower then the normal body temperature of the animal in question!).

Is this not the right number to use for TC_MAX?

Thank you!
Adam

messages.subject: Re: Upper Critical Temperature
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adam,

For endotherms, upper critical temperature refers to the air temperature, not the body temperature. See attached for a discussion about why upper critical temperature really isn't a functional trait. TC_MAX is how high you allow your animal to let its core temperature go as part of physiological thermoregulation. Does that answer your question?

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Range Wide Activity Map
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I frequently see papers using NicheMapR to calculate range or continent wide conditions (like potential activity hours) for a species in a similar way as you have done in the Heteronotia binoei paper from 2004, with resulting raster outputs across the range of a species. Despite how common this seems in the literature, I have yet to come upon a standardized methodology of applying a parameterized ectotherm model across a range to produce a raster image like this, only running it at individual points. While in theory I feel like I could come up with ways to do this, I wanted to double check that there wasn’t already some built in functionality or documentation on doing this that I may be missing that you could point me in the direction of.

Thanks in advance,

Connor Hughes
--
M.S. Biology, Austin Peay State University 2022
B.S. Wildlife and Fisheries Ecology and Conservation & GIS Technologies.
UMass Amherst College of Natural Sciences 2020
He/Him/His
